nodes.prompt:
You are on a feature branch of the oh-my-graph Go repo. Implement this task,
keeping the diff focused and matching the existing style (DESIGN.md is the
spec; English-only):
  {{ inputs.task }}
os/exec belongs to the FOUR exec seams only — runner.ClaudeCLIRunner,
verify.ShellVerifier, worktree.GitManager, browser.ExecOpener — and a fifth
spawner needs an ADR before it lands; internal/invariants enforces this.
Add or update tests. Choose a commit granularity that fits the work —
one commit per refactoring unit for refactors, per file for sweeps, per
feature slice for new code — and state your choice in the first commit
message. Commit as you go: a node timeout must never lose finished work.
Stage ONLY the files you created or modified for this task, by explicit
path (`git add <path> ...`). Never `git add -A`, `git add .`, or
`git add -u`: the working tree may hold untracked files that are not part
of this task (assets someone dropped in, scratch output), and sweeping
them into your commit is a bug.
End every commit message with the trailer
`Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>` (the attribution
convention in CONTRIBUTING.md).
Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this node's turn ends the moment you
reply, so work you promise to do afterwards never happens. Never end on
a plan to continue — report the state that is TRUE AS YOU REPLY. When
the change is committed, START your reply with the bare word DONE —
those four characters FIRST, no markdown emphasis (`**DONE**` is WRONG),
no heading, no preamble — then a one-line summary of what you changed.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the verdict, never before it:
a line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the
work is done.
If it is not finished, do NOT write DONE: start with a bare BLOCKED and
the current state.

Review findings from the previous round follow — they are empty on the
first pass. If present, fix every blocking finding before anything
else, and note that the branch already carries the previous round's
commits: amend the work, do not restart it. Items under a `Minor:` line
are not this round's to fix: leave them unless a blocking fix rewrites
the same code anyway — they reach the PR body through the review.
{{ feedback.review-verdict }}

Continue the work — or, on a retried attempt, start from the branch's
committed state — and run `make local` (build + test + vet).
If the diff touches concurrency-sensitive code or its tests
(internal/schedule, internal/runner, anything spawning goroutines or
using channels), ALSO stress those packages —
`go test <pkgs> -race -count=300` — because a flaky test passes a
single run; determinism is the claim under test.
Run every check SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for it to finish — never in the
background. Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an
interim report. If everything succeeds, your reply is exactly the four
bare characters PASS and nothing else — no markdown emphasis (`**PASS**`
is WRONG), no heading, no backticks, no preamble. Otherwise reply FAIL,
equally bare, as the very first characters, followed by the failing step.

Review the current branch's diff vs main for security issues (injection, secrets, unsafe
shell, unsafe exec, authz gaps). The e2e verdict was: {{ artifacts.e2e | inline }}.

Your own reply from the previous review round of this diff follows — it
is empty on the first pass. If present, the diff was reworked to answer
it: first check each of those findings and re-raise only the ones still
open. Raise a NEW finding only where the rework changed the code, or
where missing it last round was a real mistake — not an issue you could
have raised then and did not. An item you rated minor last round stays
minor unless the rework changed the code it is about; a blocking item
stays blocking while it is open. If every earlier finding is closed and
nothing new meets that bar, the verdict is CLEAN, or MINOR: if only
minor items remain open.
{{ self.previous }}

Finish the review BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this
node's turn ends the moment you reply, so a part of the diff you promise
to look at afterwards is never looked at. Never end on "I'll continue" —
report what you have actually judged. Judge each item by whether you
would merge with it unfixed, not by how small the fix is: an exploitable
issue is blocking; hardening with no concrete path to exploit is minor.
A reply's verdict is its worst item. START the reply with exactly one of
these three bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters, with no markdown
emphasis (`**CLEAN**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble:
  - CLEAN — you reviewed the whole diff and found no security issues.
  - MINOR: — you found something worth changing, but nothing you raise
    blocks a merge; followed by a short bulleted list, worst first.
  - FINDINGS: — at least one item you would not merge without fixing;
    followed by the blocking items as a short bulleted list, worst first,
    then any minor items under a `Minor:` line.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the token, never before it: a
line of context ahead of it fails this node even when the review is
finished.

Review the current branch's diff vs main for style, naming, and simplicity.
Also check adherence to DESIGN.md's invariants (the four exec seams, env scrub, no Agent SDK).
If the diff adds or edits test doubles or concurrency tests, also verify:
every synchronization field is actually wired (no dead channels, no
wall-clock fallback arms) and no assertion is satisfiable by a record or
node simply being absent.

Your own reply from the previous review round of this diff follows — it
is empty on the first pass. If present, the diff was reworked to answer
it: first check each of those findings and re-raise only the ones still
open. Raise a NEW finding only where the rework changed the code, or
where missing it last round was a real mistake — not a nit you could
have raised then and did not. An item you rated minor last round stays
minor unless the rework changed the code it is about; a blocking item
stays blocking while it is open. If every earlier finding is closed and
nothing new meets that bar, the verdict is CLEAN, or MINOR: if only
minor items remain open.
{{ self.previous }}

Finish the review BEFORE you reply. Your FINAL reply IS the verdict: this
node's turn ends the moment you reply, so a part of the diff you promise
to look at afterwards is never looked at. Never end on "I'll continue" —
report what you have actually judged. Judge each item by whether you
would merge with it unfixed, not by how small the fix is: a defect, wrong
behaviour, or a changed behaviour with no test is blocking; naming,
wording and simplification are minor. A reply's verdict is its worst
item. START the reply with exactly one of these three bare tokens, as the
very FIRST characters, with no markdown emphasis (`**CLEAN**` is WRONG),
no heading, no preamble:
  - CLEAN — you reviewed the whole diff and found nothing worth changing.
  - MINOR: — you found something worth changing, but nothing you raise
    blocks a merge; followed by a short bulleted list, worst first.
  - FINDINGS: — at least one item you would not merge without fixing;
    followed by the blocking items as a short bulleted list, worst first,
    then any minor items under a `Minor:` line.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the token, never before it: a
line of context ahead of it fails this node even when the review is
finished.

Two reviews of the current branch's diff follow. Do not review the diff
yourself and do not add findings of your own: your only job is to
combine the two reviewers' verdicts into one.
  Security review: {{ artifacts.review-security | inline }}
  Style review:    {{ artifacts.review-style | inline }}

Your FINAL reply IS the verdict. START it with exactly one of these three
bare tokens, as the very FIRST characters, with no markdown emphasis
(`**CLEAN**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble:
  - CLEAN — BOTH reviews start with CLEAN.
  - MINOR: — neither review starts with FINDINGS: and at least one
    starts with MINOR:. Follow the token with every minor item from
    every review that raised one, verbatim, under a `Security:` or
    `Style:` label.
  - FINDINGS: — either review starts with FINDINGS:. Follow the token
    with every blocking finding from every review that raised one,
    verbatim, under a `Security:` or `Style:` label, worst first — not
    the items a review lists under its `Minor:` line.

verify.command: rc=0; for f in "{{ artifacts.review-security }}" "{{ artifacts.review-style }}"; do if ! head -c 256 "$f" | tr -d '*_`\r' | tr '\t\n' '  ' | grep -Eq '^ *(CLEAN([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)|MINOR *:)'; then head -c 1900 "$f"; echo; rc=1; fi; done; exit $rc

nodes.prompt:
Push the current branch and open a DRAFT pull request with `gh pr create --draft`.
Put both reviews in the PR body:
  Security review: {{ artifacts.review-security | inline }}
  Style review:    {{ artifacts.review-style | inline }}
Your grant is exactly this: `git`, `gh`, Read, and writing ONE file,
`.omg-pr-body.md` in your working directory. Any other call is denied,
not asked about. A body passed inline is denied even though it starts
with `gh`: a multi-line `--body '…'`, a heredoc and a `$(…)` are all
refused. So the body goes through that file, in this order:
  1. Write the whole body to `.omg-pr-body.md` with the Write tool (if
     an earlier run left one there, Read it first, then overwrite it).
  2. Run `gh pr create --title '<one line>' --body-file .omg-pr-body.md`,
     plus any other flag asked for above (such as `--draft`).
  3. Never `git add` or commit `.omg-pr-body.md`; it is not part of the
     change.
  4. Once the PR is open, delete the file with
     `git clean -f -- .omg-pr-body.md`: a stray untracked file stops the
     run's worktree from being removed.
Every Bash call is ONE program: no `cd`, `&&`, `;`, `|`, redirect or
heredoc. To act in another directory, use `git -C <dir>`. A denied call
means the FORM was wrong, not the goal: re-issue it in the form above
before you give up on it.
Open it BEFORE you reply: your FINAL reply IS the verdict, so a PR you
promise to open afterwards is never opened. START your reply with the
bare token PR followed immediately by the pull request's URL
(`PR https://github.com/owner/repo/pull/123`) — those characters FIRST,
with no markdown emphasis (`**PR**` is WRONG), no heading, no preamble.
Anything you need to qualify goes AFTER the URL, never before it: a
line of context ahead of the token fails this node even when the PR
is open.
